newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber extends fall at close.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber extends fall at close.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices extended losses at the close due to weak consumer demand, traders said.

Chinese buyers made some inquiries for SMR 20 this morning, but nothing was concluded. Traders said Chinese buyers, seeking a fair quantity of rubber, was asking for 280 Malaysian cents a kg for April/May shipment against offer price of 282-283 cents.
"I think the Chinese were merely trying to get an indication of prices," said one trader.
But traders said fresh buying by China was likely soon as sellers were under pressure to lower their offer prices.
At the close, May RSS1 buyer was quoted by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board at 294.50 cents ($1.19) a kg, down 1.50 cents from Thursday.
May SMR 20 buyer was down three cents to 278.50 ($1.12).
Trading houses offered SMR CV at 348 cents a kg, SMR L at 328, SMR 5 at 288, SMR 10 at 283 and drum latex FOB at 235.
The INRO five-day moving average was 226.94 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on April 3 against 227.52 on April 2. The daily indicator price was 225.36 versus 225.92.
